subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Healthy Defaults in Cafeterias
description: A fast breakdown of Healthy Defaults in Cafeterias for builders.

hook.text: A school cafeteria placed fruit at eye level and fries below the counter. Fruit consumption rose 25%.

buildup.text: Wansink's smarter lunchroom initiative rearranged food placement to make healthy choices easier without restricting.

discovery.text: Putting water before soda, salad before fries, and healthy items at the start of the line shifts choices at population.

twist.text: Some of Wansink's research has been retracted for data problems. But independent replications confirmed that placement.

climax.text: Default food placement is a policy tool. What cafeterias serve first, display prominently, and position at eye level.

punchline.text: Put the apple where the cookie was. The choice changes itself.

quiz.question: How did cafeteria rearrangement increase fruit consumption?
options: By placing fruit at eye level where it was seen and reached first
By making fruit cheaper than other foods
